OPALX uses CMake and Kokkos to select the execution backend. The following
toolchain is recommended for current development and production builds:

| Dependency | Recommended version | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| GCC | 13 | Use the same host compiler throughout the dependency stack. |
| [Fortran compiler]{.getting-started-review-change} | [e.g. gfortran from GCC 13]{.getting-started-review-change} | [Required to build the fetched BLAS/LAPACK dependency.]{.getting-started-review-change} |
| OpenMPI | 4 or 5 | Either major version is suitable; use the MPI wrappers from the selected installation. |
| CUDA | 12.9 | Required only for NVIDIA GPU builds. Match the architecture setting to the target GPU. |
| CMake | 3.24 or newer | OPALX currently declares CMake 3.24 as its minimum version. |
| Git | Recent release | Used to clone OPALX and fetched dependencies. |

These are recommended versions, not a promise that every other combination is
unsupported. Accelerator builds need the matching CUDA or HIP toolchain. Other
core dependencies are obtained by the build unless installed-dependency
options are selected.

On a module-based system, a typical environment is:

```bash
module load gcc/13
module load openmpi/5  # openmpi/4 is also supported
module load cuda/12.9  # CUDA builds only
```

Module names vary between clusters. After loading them, check that `gcc`,
`mpicxx`, and `nvcc` resolve to the intended installations before configuring
the build.

## Clone the source

::: {.getting-started-review-change}
```bash
git clone --branch OPALX-1.0.0 --depth 1 https://github.com/OPALX-project/OPALX.git
cd OPALX
```

This checks out the **OPALX 1.0.0 release**, whose Git tag is
`OPALX-1.0.0`, in detached-HEAD state. All build commands below use this
checkout. To confirm the selected release, run:

```bash
git describe --tags --exact-match
# Expected: OPALX-1.0.0
```

For ongoing development, clone the default branch separately rather than
reusing a release build directory.

:::

## Configure a CPU build

For a portable single-threaded backend:

```bash
cmake -S . -B build_serial \
  -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DPLATFORMS=SERIAL
cmake --build build_serial -j 8
```

For OpenMP, use a separate build directory:

```bash
cmake -S . -B build_openmp \
  -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DPLATFORMS=OPENMP
cmake --build build_openmp -j 8
```

## Configure a GPU build

An NVIDIA A100 build uses the CUDA backend and Ampere architecture:

```bash
cmake -S . -B build_cuda \
  -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DPLATFORMS=CUDA \
  -DARCH=AMPERE80
cmake --build build_cuda -j 8
```

Select the architecture that matches the target GPU. HIP builds use
`-DPLATFORMS=HIP` and the corresponding AMD architecture.

## Enable tests

::: {.getting-started-review-change}
To build and run the unit tests for the serial backend:

```bash
cmake -S . -B build_serial \
  -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DPLATFORMS=SERIAL \
  -DOPALX_ENABLE_UNIT_TESTS=ON
cmake --build build_serial -j 8
ctest --test-dir build_serial --output-on-failure
```

For a small end-to-end check of the executable, run the regression input in
[Run a First Simulation](first-simulation.qmd#regression-smoke-test). Unit tests
and simulation regression checks serve different purposes.

:::

See [Build, Test, and CI](../developer-guide/build-test-ci.qmd) for the full
developer workflow and [Configuration Reference](../reference/configuration.qmd)
for the maintained build options.
